question: A legal dispute has been dragging on for years over the decision to award a 29-year contract worth more than EUR 2 billion to a hybrid public-private company called SIE1 to manage the Province of Catania’s integrated water services.

Both the National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANAC) and the Regulatory Authority for Energy, Networks and Environment (ARERA) have received appeals and reports concerning the concession, which was also the subject of a case brought by ANCE2 to the Regional Administrative Court of Sicily.
The resulting judgment criticised the award procedure for potentially violating competition principles and for the absence of a valid scope plan for 2024-2027.

Meanwhile, residents suspect that local councils are applying the ARERA MTI-4 water bill calculation method by means of a process that is lacking transparency – a state of affairs that could, were the proposed scope plan and pricing system to be rejected, have repercussions for NRRP financing and lead to delays in upgrading the province’s aqueducts, sewerage system and water purification facilities.
Could the Commission therefore answer the following questions: 1.
Is it aware of the Catania Water Board’s actions, and does it think that they comply with the EU’s water directives3and its legislation governing public procurement and concessions?
Will the Commission call on the competent authorities to adopt the measures needed to safeguard the planned NRRP funding measures, ensure price transparency and protect water users?

Servizi Idrici Etnei. The Association of Building Manufacturers of Italy. See the EU’s directives concerning public procurement/concessions, as well as Directive (EU) 2020/2184 on the quality of water intended for human consumption, Directive (EU) 2024/3019 on urban wastewater treatment and the Water Framework Directive’s (2000/60/EC) provisions concerning transparency, competition, planning and cost recovery.
answer: In accordance with the recast Drinking Water Directive (1) provisions, which Italy has transposed into national legislation, Member States must ensure that information on the price of drinking water is provided to the consumers, for instance by means of an invoice.

In the case of water suppliers providing more than 10 000 m 3 per day or serving at least 50 000 people, information on prices must be made accessible online, in a user friendly and customised way and information on the structure of the tariff has to be provided annually.

As regards compliance with the Concessions Directive (2), the Commission is not in a position to make an assessment based on the available information. The Commission services stand ready, however, to receive and examine further information.

The Commission will assess the completion of the projects financed by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) (3) in line with the requirements embedded in the relevant milestones and targets as outlined in the annex to the Council Implementing Decision on the approval of Italy’s recovery and resilience plan (RRP) (4). Servizi Idrici Etnei may be a beneficiary of some projects under investment M2C4.I4.
